Subtract 359 days from 1243-01-19.  
1243 is not a leap year (divisible by 4 but year < 1582, but Julian rule: divisible by 4 → leap year).  
1243 ÷ 4 = 310.75 → not divisible by 4 → not leap year.  
359 days = 365 − 6 → go back 6 days before start of year: 1243-01-19 → back 19 days to 1243-01-01, then back 340 more days into 1242.  
340 days before 1243-01-01 = 1242-01-26? Check: Jan 31 days, Feb 28 (1242 leap? 1242 ÷ 4 = 310.5 → not divisible by 4 → not leap), Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, Jun 30, Jul 31, Aug 31, Sep 30, Oct 31, Nov 30, Dec 31.  
Days remaining after 1243-01-01 back 340: 340 − 334 = 6 days before Jan 1, 1242? That’s wrong — actually going backward: from 1243-01-01, subtract 340 days = go to 1242-01-26? Let’s sum: Jan 1242 has 31 days, so 31 − 26 = 5 days into Jan 1242 means date 1242-01-26 is 340 days before 1243-01-01? Let’s count forward from 1242-01-26 to 1243-01-01: days in 1242 after Jan 26 = 5 days (Jan 27–31) = 5, then Feb 28 = 33, Mar 31 = 64, Apr 30 = 94, May 31 = 125, Jun 30 = 155, Jul 31 = 186, Aug 31 = 217, Sep 30 = 247, Oct 31 = 278, Nov 30 = 308, Dec 31 = 339, plus Jan 1, 1243 = 340 days. Yes.  
So 1243-01-19 minus 19 days = 1243-01-01, minus 340 more days = 1242-01-26.
